subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory treat OGG/Opus as unsupported input to skip/report, or should OpenClaw own an automatic transcode path to MP3/WAV before embedding?
rationale: Both options are plausible, but they have different user-facing compatibility, dependency, and maintenance costs that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow Gemini support
options.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV-only audio for Gemini embeddings, with a clear non-fatal skip or diagnostic for OGG/Opus files.

options.title: Own transcoding
options.body: Add an ffmpeg-backed conversion path for unsupported audio formats before Gemini embedding, including dependency detection, failure handling, and tests.

options.title: Defer behind broader multimodal design
options.body: Keep this open under the broader multimodal memory direction until maintainers settle provider-specific media handling across formats.

recommendation.title: Narrow Gemini support
recommendation.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV-only audio for Gemini embeddings, with a clear non-fatal skip or diagnostic for OGG/Opus files.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision lands closest to the shipped multimodal memory extraPaths implementation and docs boundary introduced in the merged memory PR.
